Revised assessment incorporating literature: The statement is hawkish and vigilant. It acknowledges downside momentum in activity but emphasizes elevated and skewed inflation risks, consistent with inflation-at-risk evidence post-pandemic and amid the Ukraine energy shock (e.g., 2024 work on “Inflation at risk”). The focus on “broader price pressures” aligns with research highlighting markups’ contribution to inflation beyond pure cost-push (2023 work on interest rates, profits, and markups) and with pandemic-related measurement/weighting effects observed internationally (2022 analysis of COVID-19 inflation weighting in Israel). The policy response—raising the funds rate to 2.25–2.50% and continuing balance sheet reduction—is in line with rule-based prescriptions (Taylor rule adherence as in Papell, Molodtsova, and Nikolsko-Rzhevskyy, 2008) given high inflation and low unemployment, and QT implies additional tightening via term-premium channels highlighted in term-structure research (Cochrane-Piazzesi). Literature on monetary policy shocks (Romer and Romer) suggests such anti-inflation moves are near-term contractionary but credibility-enhancing for inflation expectations. Net tone: cautious/negative on the macro outlook with strong anti-inflation resolve. Adjusting for these insights, the sentiment is slightly more negative than before.
